item.description: Treatment in the intensive care unit (ICU) is usually predicated on curative treatment, but continuing all available treatment options may not always be beneficial for the patient or in line with their wishes. item.title: Swedish Consensus Recommendation for Follow-Up After ICU Stay.
item.description: A substantial proportion of intensive care unit (ICU) survivors experience long-term physical, psychological and cognitive impairments after critical illness. However, methods for identifying patients in need of post-ICU support vary widely. As a result, many patients are left without access to established rehabilitation pathways. item.title: Endpoint-specific mortality associated with malignancy among adults with sepsis or septic shock: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: Sepsis is a major global health challenge and increasingly affects patients with complex conditions such as malignancy. Prior studies suggest higher mortality in this population, but interpretation is limited by aggregation of heterogeneous endpoints. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to clarify endpoint-specific prognostic associations between malignancy and mortality in adults with sepsis or septic shock. item.title: Management of Patients After Cardiac Arrest.
item.description: Cardiac arrest remains a significant cause of morbidity and mortality, although contemporary care now enables potential survival with good neurologic outcome. The core acute management goals for survivors of cardiac arrest are to provide organ support, sustain adequate hemodynamics, and evaluate the underlying cause of the cardiac arrest. item.title: Causal mediation analysis of contact with COVID-19 patients and burnout syndrome in physiotherapists in Japan: secondary analysis of a multicentre observational study.
item.description: This study looked at Japanese physiotherapists who worked with COVID-19 patients and found that direct contact with patients contributed to burnout, but this effect was partly buffered by appreciation and respect from patients and colleagues. The study suggests that organisational resources, such as reimbursement for care, may also play a role in burnout. Burnout prevalence was 19.4% among the physiotherapists.

item.title: Bedside pharmacist interventions for managing intravenous drug incompatibilities in critically ill patients.
item.description: Patients admitted to intensive care units are at increased risk of intravenous drug incompatibilities, owing to polypharmacy and the limited number of available venous access devices. To evaluate bedside pharmacist interventions for managing drug incompatibilities identified during intravenous administration in intensive care unit patients. A cross-sectional study with prospective data collection was conducted between June and December 2025 in five intensive care units of a university hospital.

item.description: Hospital-acquired anemia (HAA), which negatively affects morbidity, mortality, and resource use, is a common iatrogenic effect of hospitalization, especially in intensive care units. item.description: Medical television dramas shape public perceptions of cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR). The Pitt has been praised for its clinical realism but has not been systematically evaluated. We assessed adherence of televised CPR to current European Resuscitation Council (ERC) and American Heart Association (AHA) guidelines. item.description: As Intensive Care Unit (ICU) survival improves, attention has shifted towards patients' psychological well-being and recovery. item.description: High-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) therapy is often used in critical care, but its effects on swallowing function remain unclear. item.description: Delirium is a common neuropsychiatric complication among critically ill patients, particularly those who are mechanically ventilated. item.description: Emotional intelligence (EI) is critical in intensive care unit (ICU) nursing, where nurses face high stress, clinical instability and emotionally demanding situations.
